score: the probability from summing hundreds of small trees
how: Every tree in the ensemble looks at the client and adds a small amount to their log-odds of subscribing; the total is turned into a probability with the sigmoid function. Because hundreds of trees each contribute, almost every client gets a different score, so the list is a fine-grained ranking of individual clients.
steps: Each tree adds or subtracts a little, scaled by the learning rate
Convert the sum to a probability with the sigmoid
Sort clients by probability; call down the list
summary: Calling the top 20% of clients by the probability from summing hundreds of small trees (1,648 calls) reaches 67% of all subscribers, with 38% of calls ending in a subscription — 3.3× calling at random.
caveat: Much of this ranking is about when a client was called: among clients called under the same economic conditions its AUC falls from 0.811 to 0.606 (within the same month: 0.748). A bank choosing whom to call this week works within one period, so expect less separation than the table suggests. Offline estimate on a random split of 2008–2010 data, not a live campaign.
